title: Katchatheevu and the “Trash” Question!
translatorNote: This translation is intended to carry Kalaignar's voice into clear, contemporary English rather than recast the letter as literary or academic prose. It preserves the source's argument, political directness, rhetorical questions, repetition, irony, factual detail, and paragraph order. Names, dates, figures, quotations, and intentional English expressions are retained. Where Tamil idiom cannot be reproduced literally without sounding unnatural, the English follows its sense and rhetorical force without adding claims absent from the source. The original Tamil is reproduced in full below the translation and remains the authoritative text. `Udanpirappē` is retained in Tamil transliteration rather than flattened into “brother,” “sister,” or “comrade.” Literally evoking “one born alongside me,” Kalaignar uses it as a distinctive address of shared identity, equality, affection, and solidarity within the movement. Letter-specific notes: 1. The title plays on the sound of **Katchatheevu** and `கச்சடா` (*kachadā*), a disparaging word meaning trash, filth or rubbish. “Trash question” preserves both the insult and the wordplay. 2. **Archanai** literally means a ritual offering or recital of names in worship; Kalaignar uses it sarcastically for a sustained shower of abuse. 3. The source reproduces the 29 June 1974 English letter verbatim. Its spelling `Kachativu` and lineation are retained. 4. “The difference between butter and lime” is a Tamil idiom for recognising a genuine thing from a deceptively similar but harmful substitute.
paragraphs: Apparently fearing that journalists might write, “Chief Minister Jayalalithaa has gone to Kodanadu to rest,” she makes sure that some statement or other appears in her name in the newspapers every day. The people of Tamil Nadu are apparently expected to believe that Ammaiyar sits at Kodanadu, consults officials and prepares and dispatches these statements! Are the people of Tamil Nadu such simpletons? Do they not know the truth?

In that sequence, our Chief Minister—who settled the Neyveli share-sale issue and the workers’ strike entirely through statements—seems yesterday to have found no subject for another statement. Not only that: on seeing detailed reports in all the newspapers of 17 July, including The Hindu, stating that the Supreme Court had admitted the case I filed seeking the retrieval of Katchatheevu and had directed the Union Government to respond, she could not bear it. She picked up her pen and produced eight pages accusing me of betrayal over Katchatheevu.

One would have to count how many times Ammaiyar has already issued statements alleging that I betrayed Tamil Nadu on this issue. Each time, she begins piling up charges that the Union Government and I joined together and handed Katchatheevu away.

If anyone in the Opposition says anything about the Chief Minister, defamation cases immediately fly. But she may speak as abusively as she wishes about Opposition leaders, and no one may question her. She lists Karunanidhi’s “first betrayal”, “second betrayal” and “third betrayal”; calls them deceptive dramas and eyewash; speaks of selfishness, “worshipping the sun after losing one’s eyesight”, and mere tokenism. These are the “beautiful Tamil expressions” born of her political culture and habitually used by her.

Why has Chief Minister Jayalalithaa poured so many pages of such bitter abuse upon me? Did I write that she had done nothing about Katchatheevu? No. I did not even enter into what she had or had not done. All I did was file a case in the Supreme Court seeking Union Government action on Katchatheevu. Even that was not the offence. The offence was that the Supreme Court admitted the case and the newspapers reported it. Can news connected with me appear, rather than news only about her?

Having issued an eight-page statement accusing me of betrayal, should I not answer it? Two months ago, on 3 May 2013, Chief Minister Jayalalithaa suddenly moved a resolution on Katchatheevu in the Legislative Assembly, spoke at length and had it adopted. From beginning to end, the speech consisted of an “archanai”—a ritual shower of abuse—directed at me.

Do you know why she suddenly remembered Katchatheevu then? The reason was the resolution adopted at the TESO meeting held at Anna Arivalayam on 15 April 2013. Its concluding passage said: “TESO has decided to approach the Supreme Court to have the 1974 agreement annulled and to have Katchatheevu declared a part of India.”

I ask Ammaiyar, who says that I betrayed Tamil Nadu over Katchatheevu: you accuse me of doing nothing to retrieve it. Yet the Supreme Court case that has now caused your anger was filed by me precisely to retrieve Katchatheevu. Is that too a betrayal?

Was it I who swore in the 1991 Independence Day speech, “I shall certainly retrieve Katchatheevu”? Twenty-two years have passed since she made that vow. What has she achieved? On 15 August 1991, was it I or Jayalalithaa who thundered: “This Government is prepared to argue with the Union Government to retrieve Katchatheevu and, if necessary, to struggle”? Having issued that challenge, what justice is there in accusing me of neither struggling nor lifting even a straw, as though she herself had uprooted a pillar?

Speaking in this same Assembly on 20 April 1992, did Jayalalithaa not say: “We passed a resolution here seeking the retrieval of Katchatheevu and sent it to the Union Government. But retrieving Katchatheevu does not appear to be something that can happen in the near future”? Having spoken as though placing a full stop on the issue, what name should be given to her statement accusing me of doing nothing?

She made all these allegations in the Assembly two months ago, and I answered them in detail then. I explained that the DMK had never accepted or agreed to the handing over of Katchatheevu; that the DMK Government too had repeatedly raised the issue and asked for its retrieval; and that it had consistently pointed out the impairment of fishermen’s rights and sought remedies. Is it right for Jayalalithaa to repeat the same allegations even after that explanation?
In that reply I cited her own letter of 30 September 1994, written as Chief Minister to Prime Minister P. V. Narasimha Rao:
“The ceding of this tiny island to the Island Nation had been done by the Government of India in the interest of better bilateral relations.”

In other words, she justified the handing over of the small island of Katchatheevu to Sri Lanka as being in the interest of better relations between India and Sri Lanka. I asked whether she had written this or not. Why has she still not answered?

Jayalalithaa asks: “Even though Karunanidhi knew before the agreement was signed that India was going to hand over Katchatheevu, why did he take no immediate action?” How many times will she ask the same question?

Immediately after the agreement was signed on 28 June 1974, did I not convene an all-party meeting at the Secretariat in Chennai on 29 June and have a resolution adopted? The AIADMK refused even then to sign in support of that resolution. On that same day, 29 June 1974, I wrote to the Prime Minister:
Dear Prime Minister,

On behalf of the Government of Tamil Nadu and on behalf of the people of Tamil Nadu, I am constrained to express our deep sense of disappointment over the recent Indo-Sri Lanka Agreement, according to which, Sri Lanka’s claim to Kachativu has been conceded by the Government of India.
May I express the hope that you will take into consideration the decision contained in the Resolution and take appropriate action?
Is this evidence that I handed Katchatheevu away? Is this the mark of betrayal?

Is it false that the DMK conducted protest demonstrations throughout Tamil Nadu on 24 July 1974? Did I not personally attend meetings in Thanjavur district as Chief Minister? When Parliament discussed the issue on 23 July 1974, did DMK member R. Sezhiyan not say: “We will not accept the handing over to Sri Lanka of Katchatheevu, which belongs to Tamil Nadu”? Did DMK member S. S. Marisamy not say in the Rajya Sabha: “The Union Government entered into this agreement unilaterally, without consulting the Tamil Nadu Government; this is undemocratic”?
At the Assembly sitting that followed, on 21 August 1974, I moved this Government resolution:

“This House expresses its deep regret over the decision taken by the Union Government on Katchatheevu, which belongs to India and over which Tamil Nadu possesses close rights. It urges the Union Government to reconsider the matter, seek to revise the agreement with Sri Lanka so that India’s sovereignty over Katchatheevu is retained, and respect the feelings of the people of Tamil Nadu.”
Are these documentary proofs of betrayal?

Jayalalithaa’s next argument is this: “Karunanidhi says that in 1974 he learnt from newspapers that Katchatheevu had been ceded and was shocked. But in 2013 he says that certain clauses were inserted before the agreement was completed because of his intervention.” She used the same words in the Assembly in May, and I answered them fully then. Yet she repeats them in yesterday’s statement.
The TESO resolution of 15 April 2013 states:

“When the 1974 agreement was being concluded, the DMK Government strongly opposed it from the outset. When the agreement was nevertheless signed, the DMK Government insisted that, at a minimum, clauses should be included preserving Tamil Nadu fishermen’s right to fish in the Katchatheevu area and their right to dry their nets there. Those clauses were accordingly included.”

Jayalalithaa further spits venom in her statement, alleging that after losing office Karunanidhi revived TESO, convened meetings, adopted resolutions and filed a Supreme Court case only for political gain; that these were attempts to deceive the people of Tamil Nadu and cover up his own error. None of my actions deceives Tamil Nadu; they safeguard Tamil interests.

Jayalalithaa moved a resolution in the Assembly on 16 April 2002 demanding that LTTE leader Prabhakaran be arrested and brought to India. Now she adopts Assembly resolutions claiming to support Sri Lankan Tamils. That is the betrayal that deceives the people of Tamil Nadu.

When innocent Tamils were massacred in Sri Lanka, Jayalalithaa declared in the Assembly: “In war, it is natural for innocent civilians to be killed.” Now she issues statements professing concern for Sri Lankan Tamils and Katchatheevu. That is an act that deceives Tamil Nadu.

She repeatedly asks why Karunanidhi, while in office, did not lift even a straw to retrieve Katchatheevu. I asked her: she herself governed from 1991 to 1996, from 2001 to 2006 and again from 2011; why did she not retrieve it? Why does her long statement contain no answer?

Jayalalithaa has filed a Supreme Court case on Katchatheevu. I too have filed one on behalf of TESO. Yet she says: “The people of Tamil Nadu know well that Mr Karunanidhi did not file the Katchatheevu case in the Supreme Court for Tamil Nadu fishermen or for the welfare of Tamils.” That is Jayalalithaa!
“Jayalalithaa filed her Supreme Court case solely for Tamil Nadu fishermen and Tamil welfare—please believe it!” That is Karunanidhi!

Jayalalithaa says: “No one can ever deceive the people of Tamil Nadu.” Yes, that is true. No one can ever deceive them. They certainly will not be deceived by anyone. The people of Tamil Nadu know the difference between butter and lime.
With affection, M.K. 20 July 2013
